content.overview: Article 200 provides that when a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly (or by both Houses where there is a Council), it shall be presented to the Governor, who shall declare either that he assents, or that he withholds assent, or that he reserves the Bill for the consideration of the President. The Governor may return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration; if passed again and presented, the Governor shall not withhold assent. The Governor shall not assent to, but shall reserve for the President, any Bill that would in the Governor’s opinion so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger the position which that Court is by the Constitution designed to fill.
content.glance: Governor: assent / withhold / reserve for President. May return non-Money Bill once; after re-passage cannot withhold. Must reserve Bills that endanger High Court’s constitutional position.
content.study:
Article 200 is the State counterpart of Article 111, with an additional mandatory reservation for Bills affecting the High Court’s constitutional position.

Options when a Bill is presented:
1. Assent.
2. Withhold assent.
3. Reserve for the consideration of the President.

First proviso: return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration (with optional recommended amendments); after the House(s) pass it again and present it, the Governor shall not withhold assent.

Second proviso: shall not assent to, but shall reserve for the President, any Bill which in the Governor’s opinion would so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger the position which that Court is by the Constitution designed to fill.

Examination: three options; return non-Money Bill once; mandatory HC-protection reservation; link Art 201 (President’s action on reserved Bills).

sections.heading: Governor’s options
sections.body:
1. Assent.
2. Withhold assent.
3. Reserve for the President.
4. Return non-Money Bill once for reconsideration; after re-passage, shall not withhold assent.
5. Must reserve (shall not assent to) Bills that would endanger the High Court’s constitutional position.
